name: Cendre Blue
lede: Cendre blue, from the French for ashes, is an old name for a pale copper-based blue, the pigment more often called blue verditer.

sections.title: Ashes blue
sections.body:
The Pigment Compendium lists *ashes blue* and *Cendres blue* among the historical names for blue verditer, a synthetic copper carbonate blue [1]. Weber (1923) gives cendre blue and cenere blue as generic synonyms for blue copper carbonates, a group that also includes azurite [2]. The English form *sanders blue* is probably a corruption of the French, according to Harley (1982) [2].

Verditer is not the same as *verdeterre*, which is green earth [2]. Bremen blue is a related name, more often applied to copper hydroxide [1][2]. See [[bremen-blue]], [[cadet-blue]] and [[blue]] [3]. The Compendium also lists *mountain blue* among the historical names for blue verditer, so the old terms overlap with azurite names [1][2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this pale blue in only 7 of 23,531 paintings, as photographed [4]. The swatch is #57B0CA, close to a sky blue [3][4].
